questions.text_clean:
5. [Maximum mark: 16]
The exponential series is given by $\mathrm{e}^x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n!}$.
(a) Find the set of values of $x$ for which the series is convergent. [4 marks]
(b) (i) Show, by comparison with an appropriate geometric series, that $\mathrm{e}^x-1<\frac{2x}{2-x}$, for $0<x<2$.
(ii) Hence show that $\mathrm{e}<\left(\frac{2n+1}{2n-1}\right)^n$, for $n\in\mathbb{Z}^+$. [6 marks]
(c) (i) Write down the first three terms of the Maclaurin series for $1-\mathrm{e}^{-x}$ and explain why you are able to state that $1-\mathrm{e}^{-x}>x-\frac{x^2}{2}$, for $0<x<2$.
(ii) Deduce that $\mathrm{e}>\left(\frac{2n^2}{2n^2-2n+1}\right)^n$, for $n\in\mathbb{Z}^+$. [4 marks]
(d) Letting $n=1000$, use the results in parts (b) and (c) to calculate the value of e correct to as many decimal places as possible. [2 marks]
